Victorian Liberal MP Moira Deeming is looking for an urgent court injunction against the party’s state president in a last-ditch effort to retain her spot on the ticket for the November state election.

The upper house MP will on Friday night face Liberal Party executives as they decide if she retains preselection.

But Ms Deeming has filed court proceedings against the Liberal Party and state president Brian Loughnane, with the matter briefly called and then adjourned in the Supreme Court on Friday morning.

Justice Kerri Judd called for more information from lawyers representing the Liberal Party executives and adjourned the matter to 1pm on Friday. Neither Ms Deeming nor Mr Loughnane were in court on Friday morning.

​Victorian Liberal MP Moira Deeming has accused former opposition leader Matthew Guy of physically assaulting her at a community event in May. ​Mr Guy has denied the allegation and is considering legal advice to sue his colleague for defamation.

Justice Judd told the court she was not being asked to rule on Victoria Police’s decision not to charge Ms Deeming’s colleague Matthew Guy, a remark that Ms Deeming’s lawyer agreed with.

“Yes, we don’t seek the court’s intervention on the underlying dispute,” herbarrister Ganesh Jegatheesan said.

Justice Kidd also told the court “a number of barristers unconnected to the case” had requested video links to the urgent injunction hearing.

One ground Ms Deeming’s motion relied on was bias, her lawyer confirmed, and Justice Kerr agreed to release Ms Deeming’s initial motion for an injunction to the media – a document that was not distributed before the 1pm resumption.

Lawyer for the Liberal Party and its president, Marcus Clarke KC, in the morning told the court “it’s quite a narrow dispute”, and a substantive hearing would likely take less than one day in court.

Justice Judd directed lawyers for the Liberal Party to file more information with the court, adjourned to 1pm on Friday, and indicated the court could set down a time for a substantive hearing “in a very short period of time”.

The Liberal Party state executive meeting on Friday night is expected to disendorse Ms Deeming.

Ms Deeming’s court action seeks an injunction to halt that meeting.

Moves from the state party powerbrokers to disendorse Ms Deeming’s preselection come after the MP refused to apologise to the former leader, Mr Guy, for accusing him of putting her in a headlock at a public event.

Police investigated the incident and found no offence was committed.

Grainy CCTV footage shows Mr Guy placing a hand on Ms Deeming’s back.

After police declined to proceed and charge Mr Guy, Ms Deeming released a statement through her lawyer saying she misunderstood the term “headlock” and maintained she acted in good faith to describe what happened.

The party’s legal affairs spokesman, James Newbury, said opposition leader Jess Wilson had asked Ms Deeming to apologise.

“Jess Wilson and Matthew Guy asked for an unqualified apology. Moira Deeming released a statement saying that she was not willing to apologise. Therefore, there will not be a meeting between Jess Wilson and Moira Deeming,” Mr Newbury said on Tuesday.

“The party is now working on the next action it will take.”

Friday’s court case is the third legal action Ms Deeming has been involved in against fellow Liberals since being elected in 2022.

She successfully sued then-opposition leader John Pesutto for defaming her.

Five current and former Liberal state executives launched legal action against the party over its decision to pay Mr Pesutto’s legal debts; Ms Deeming did not launch that case but is a defendant.
